case.name: Meshullam

A.name: Meshullam
A.line: stood at Ezra's left hand as he read the law to the people (NEH 8:4)
A.notes: The priest who sealed the covenant (NEH 10:7), the chief of the people who sealed it (NEH 10:20) and the head of the house of Ginnethon (NEH 12:16) are held apart; the text does not say whether any of them is this man.

kjv.NEH 8:4: And Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, and Shema, and Anaiah, and Urijah, and Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, and Mishael, and Malchiah, and Hashum, and Hashbadana, Zechariah, and Meshullam.

B.name: Meshullam

family: companion-of ezra (Ezra, son of Seraiah (EZR 7:1), scribe skilled in the Law (EZR 7:6)

disputed_verses.KJV NEH 8:4: And Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, and Shema, and Anaiah, and Urijah, and Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, and Mishael, and Malchiah, and Hashum, and Hashbadana, Zechariah, and Meshullam.

first_reader_said: NEH 8:4: Both records are Meshullam standing at Ezra's left hand at the reading of the law, with nothing else to tell them apart.

why: Both records identify the same Meshullam, named last among those standing at Ezra’s left hand in NEH 8:4. Keep B because its association with Ezra is supported by that verse, whereas A’s attribution to Levi is not established there.
